trust_decision.summary: Untrusted: the 'url' of a 'gml' map layer in the print request body is fetched and its text handed to the geotools XSD Parser with entity resolution enabled; the fix decides that a GML document fetched from that request-supplied URL must be parsed with DOCTYPE/external-entity resolution disabled and must not be echoed back in errors - at GmlLayer.java:122-126 (pre-validation of the fetched string) and GmlLayer.java:189-193 (EntityResolver2 on the shared Parser).

landing_point.why: An engineer reading 'MapFish Print has XXE' greps for XML parsing and lands on the parser.parse(new StringReader(gmlData)) calls; the only text the running system shows about a bad document is PrintException("Failed to parse Gml32 " + gmlData) at :185, which points at parseGml32. The published fix actually lands one step upstream at the fetch (:122-126) and in the shared parser factory (:189-193).

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /print/report.{format} or POST /print/{appId}/report.{format} (MapPrinterServlet.java:659, :542) with a map layer {"type":"gml","url":...}
fix_sites.module_kind: map layer plugin, request-driven ingest (fetch then validate)
parser factory shared by the gml2, gml3 and gml3.2 parsers (entity resolver)
error reporting inside the layer plugin (gmlData removed from the exception messages)

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate GML that declares an external schema through xsi:schemaLocation must still be resolvable through the registered CachingUrihandler; a fix that switches off external DTD/schema access on the geotools Parser (or drops/replaces the URI handler) instead of only blocking entities breaks the project's own GML fixtures, which all carry a remote schemaLocation.

O6_input_shapes: DOCTYPE with an internal general entity referenced in element text (the published malicious-doctype.gml case)
DOCTYPE with a SYSTEM external DTD (load-external-dtd false, ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD "")
parameter entities and external general entities (external-general-entities / external-parameter-entities false)
the three EntityResolver2 callback shapes: getExternalSubset, 4-arg resolveEntity, 2-arg resolveEntity
the same payload delivered as an http(s) URL, a file URL inside the config dir, or a data: URL - all pass through the single fetch in createFeatureSource

O8b_injection_room.sibling: inline raw-GML support on GmlParam.url, a second ingest route into the same Parser
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The field javadoc already advertises 'An url to the gml or the raw Gml data' while only the URL branch is implemented (GmlLayer.java:119-135), so a maintainer adding the documented inline branch is natural and would bypass the fetch-site validation at :126.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a GML branch in autoTreat() next to the GeoJSON one, parsing request-supplied features with the same geotools Parser
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: FeaturesParser is the sibling ingester for request-supplied feature data (used by the 'features' attribute and GeoJsonLayer) and already mixes URL and inline-string ingest; extending it to the GML format the project already supports is an ordinary feature request.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new feature-source layer type (e.g. wfs) that fetches a URL and parses the returned GML with GmlLayer-like code
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The plugin base class exists precisely to add feature-source layers; every such layer takes request JSON params, so another GML-consuming plugin is the obvious next one.

O9_family: XML external entity (XXE) / improper restriction of XML external entity references (CWE-611)

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 9.3.1 wrapper (gradlew, build.gradle:14-17, sourceCompatibility 21 at build.gradle:55-58), checkstyle + spotbugs; no Maven pom
O10_build.project_tests: core/src/test/java/org/mapfish/print/processor/map/CreateMapProcessorFlexibleScaleBBoxGmlTest.java (testExecute renders spearfish gml v2 and v3.1.1 through a mocked HTTP factory, :45-90); fixtures under core/src/test/resources/map-data/gml/; the added XXE test would use the same mock factory plus a DOCTYPE fixture.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set the entity resolver on the gmlV32Parser instance inside parseGml32 - the path the report's error message names - and strip gmlData from the messages, leaving the shared createParser factory and the gml2/gml3 parsers expanding entities.

out_of_scope_notes: core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/output/AbstractJasperReportOutputFormat.java:379-386 parses jrxml with a default DocumentBuilderFactory (no DOCTYPE hardening), but the input is the template configuration, not request data - different sink, not pursued.

core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/processor/map/NorthArrowGraphic.java:335-339 parses an SVG north-arrow graphic with Batik, and core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/map/image/ImageLayer.java:181-189 decodes a request-supplied image URL with ImageIO (SVG goes through Batik's XML parser) - a sibling XXE surface outside the GML protection this advisory is about, not pursued.

core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/map/geotools/CachingUrihandler.java:46-61 still lets the GML parser resolve xsi:schemaLocation references (outbound HTTP, and file: paths out of the schema cache); the fix leaves that open by design, and it is resource fetch/SSRF rather than XXE file disclosure, so not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured (no shell in this session); the tree has 572 Java files plus binary test fixtures and a bundled Cadastra.jar, so it is judged well above 5 MB rather than under it.

The six fix commits are the same patch applied to several release branches (differences are javax/jakarta annotations, add/addFirst, JUnit 4/5, and the Values constructor arity), not six independent changes; many_fix_commits is set on the literal count.

Whether the existing GML render tests need network to resolve the xsi:schemaLocation URLs (localhost:9876, www.openplans.org) through CachingUrihandler was not checked; the layer URL itself is served by the in-process mock factory, and the XXE behaviour would be exercised offline.

No request-controlled XML parse other than the GML layer was found in the pinned tree (SLDParserPlugin.java:99-104 already sets disallow-doctype-decl), so O2 and O8 are empty; single_site was not set because the published fix changes three methods and two messages, but the effect is confined to one class and one sink.
